name: Database schema: `derived`
desc:
The schema of the SQLite database browl calls `derived`, which holds data derived from the loaded ontology. These pages are generated from the code by [tbls](https://github.com/k1LoW/tbls) (`make schema-docs`; overview in [docs/SCHEMA.md](../../SCHEMA.md)): edit `.tbls/derived.yml`, not them.

browl builds one such SQLite file per load, `DATA_DIR/derived/{generation}.sqlite3`, from bulk SPARQL queries against the ontology in Fuseki. It holds whatever needs the whole ontology (entities and their URLs, names, hierarchies, counts, search), so pages never query Fuseki for it. It's a cache: rebuilt on every load, never migrated ([DESIGN.md 2.5](../../DESIGN.md#25-derived-data-pre-caching)).

tables.name: meta
tables.comment: What the database was built from (browl.derived.Meta), one row. generation is read from a file built by any browl, so it keeps its name.

columns.name: id
columns.comment: Always 1, so the table has one row.

columns.name: generation
columns.comment: The load job's generation number; the file is current only for that generation.

columns.name: ontology_iri
columns.comment: The ontology's IRI, from its own graph; NULL if it has none.

columns.name: version_iri
columns.comment: Its owl:versionIRI; NULL if it has none.

columns.name: title
columns.comment: Its title (dcterms:title, dc:title, then NAME_PROPERTIES); NULL if it has none, and pages show the IRI.

columns.name: version_info
columns.comment: Its owl:versionInfo; NULL if it has none.

columns.name: reasoner
columns.comment: The reasoner the load ran (browl.jobtypes.Reasoner).

columns.name: loaded_at
columns.comment: When the load job started, ISO 8601 with a time zone; a rebuild after a restart keeps it.

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE meta (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK (id = 1),
    generation INTEGER NOT NULL,
    ontology_iri TEXT,
    version_iri TEXT,
    title TEXT,
    version_info TEXT,
    reasoner TEXT NOT NULL,
    loaded_at TEXT NOT NULL
)

tables.name: build_key
tables.comment: The build keys the file was built with, one per component (browl.precache.keys, DESIGN.md 2.5). The file is current only if they're the components and keys the running browl computes, so a change to the code or settings that build it rebuilds it. Read from a file built by any browl, so it keeps its name and columns; a file without it, built before build keys, isn't current.

columns.name: component
columns.comment: What the key covers: schema (browl.derived.SCHEMA and INDEXES), meta (the ontology header and the meta row), or a pre-caching hook, by name (e.g. entities).

columns.name: key
columns.comment: A SHA-256, in hex, of what the component depends on: for schema, its SQL; for the others, their code (their browl modules' syntax trees, without docstrings, the files they load through sparql_file, the third-party distributions' versions, Python's version) and the values of the settings they declare.

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE build_key (
    component TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    key TEXT NOT NULL
) WITHOUT ROWID

tables.name: entity
tables.comment: The ontology itself and every declared class and property, with the URL its IRI implies (DESIGN.md 2.3, browl.urls), filled by the entities pre-caching hook. An IRI declared with several types (punning) has a row for each. Several IRIs can share a URL, e.g. the http and https forms of one (U-15).

columns.name: id
columns.comment: The entity's number, dense, in the order the entity list returned it; the other tables refer to it.

columns.name: iri
columns.comment: The entity's IRI, as the ontology has it.

columns.name: type
columns.comment: "Its type (browl.derived.EntityType): ontology, class, object_property, data_property or annotation_property."

columns.name: path
columns.comment: Its URL's path from the site's root (BASE_URL), in URI form (non-ASCII percent-encoded as UTF-8). For a fallback URL, the path and query string, /{RESERVED_PREFIX}/iri?iri={the percent-encoded IRI}.

columns.name: fragment
columns.comment: The fragment of a hash IRI's URL, in URI form; NULL for any other, and for every fallback URL.

columns.name: display_name
columns.comment: Its display name (DESIGN.md 2.7): its best name value, else its CURIE, else its IRI; for the ontology, its title (meta.title) if it has one.

columns.name: curie
columns.comment: Its CURIE, from the longest namespace in the prefix table that covers it; NULL if none does.

indexes.name: entity_path
indexes.def: CREATE INDEX entity_path ON entity (path, fragment)

indexes.name: entity_iri_type
indexes.def: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX entity_iri_type ON entity (iri, type)

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE entity (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    iri TEXT NOT NULL,
    type TEXT NOT NULL,
    path TEXT NOT NULL,
    fragment TEXT,
    display_name TEXT,
    curie TEXT
)

tables.name: name_value
tables.comment: Each entity's values of the name properties (NAME_PROPERTIES), for display names: one row per value and name property, direct if the entity has it under that property itself, else entailed through rdfs:subPropertyOf; stored in entity order.

columns.name: entity
columns.comment: The entity (entity.id).

columns.name: property
columns.comment: The name property's IRI.

columns.name: value
columns.comment: The value's lexical form.

columns.name: normalized
columns.comment: The value normalized for search (browl.names.normalize).

columns.name: language
columns.comment: The value's language tag, lowercased; NULL if it has none.

columns.name: direct
columns.comment: 1 if the entity has the value under this property itself, 0 if under one of its sub-properties.

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE name_value (
    entity INTEGER NOT NULL,
    property TEXT NOT NULL,
    value TEXT NOT NULL,
    normalized TEXT NOT NULL,
    language TEXT,
    direct INTEGER NOT NULL
)

tables.name: annotation_value
tables.comment: Every string or language-tagged value of each annotation property (declared, OWL's built-in ones, or a name property) on a declared entity, for search: one row per value, under the property it's asserted with, so an entailed value is stored once, as itself; stored in entity order. The lane index (search_value) holds the name-like properties' values, and P-46's full-text index the prose ones'.

columns.name: entity
columns.comment: The entity (entity.id).

columns.name: property
columns.comment: The property it's asserted with (search_property.id).

columns.name: value
columns.comment: The value's lexical form.

columns.name: language
columns.comment: The value's language tag, lowercased; NULL if it has none.

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE annotation_value (
    entity INTEGER NOT NULL,
    property INTEGER NOT NULL,
    value TEXT NOT NULL,
    language TEXT
)

tables.name: search_property
tables.comment: The annotation properties search knows (DESIGN.md 2.6, Every annotation property): each one with values in annotation_value; each name, label and synonym property even without, so a default search reaches its sub-properties' values; and each super-property of one with values, so it can be chosen for them. Each is name-like or prose (browl.precache.values.classify).

columns.name: id
columns.comment: The property's id, which annotation_value, search_value, search_lane and common_value use.

columns.name: iri
columns.comment: Its IRI.

columns.name: prose
columns.comment: 1 if it's prose (definitions, comments, notes), which the lane index leaves out; 0 if it's name-like (labels, synonyms, IDs, cross-references).

columns.name: by_default
columns.comment: 1 if a search that names no properties searches it: the name, label and synonym properties, and any other name-like one whose values are on fewer than browl.precache.values.NAME_REUSE entities each, on average.

columns.name: value_count
columns.comment: How many values it has in annotation_value; 0 for one listed only for its sub-properties.

indexes.name: search_property_iri
indexes.def: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX search_property_iri ON search_property (iri)

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE search_property (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    iri TEXT NOT NULL,
    prose INTEGER NOT NULL,
    by_default INTEGER NOT NULL,
    value_count INTEGER NOT NULL
)

tables.name: sub_property
tables.comment: Each property's sub-properties, transitively (rdfs:subPropertyOf), among those in search_property, stored in key order: a search of a property with entailed values also searches these, after its own.

columns.name: property
columns.comment: The property (search_property.id).

columns.name: sub
columns.comment: One of its sub-properties, directly or not (search_property.id).

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE sub_property (
    property INTEGER NOT NULL,
    sub INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (property, sub)
) WITHOUT ROWID

tables.name: search_value
tables.comment: The search index (browl.search.SqliteSearch): each name-like property's value (search_property.prose = 0) that isn't empty once normalized, keyed in the order search ranks values within a lane, with a word row for each later word start (browl.search.word_starts), keyed by the normalized value from that word on, so a query matches the start of any word: for words within the first browl.search.MAX_QUERY_CHARS normalized characters, keyed by at most that many, so a value's rows are bounded however long it is. The rows that share the key's first four columns (type, property, language_rank, word) form a lane, ordered within by length, normalized value, value, entity, then word_start. A query orders the lanes it reads by its own walk of the properties, seeks its matches in one lane and of one length at a time, shortest first, so it never sorts them. The key holds at most browl.search.KEY_CHARS characters of each value, so a query seeks at most that many lengths per lane however long the values are. Language ranks are by LANGUAGE_RANKING as built, which the search hook's build key covers. Of an entity's values that differ only in language tags that rank alike, one row is kept.

columns.name: type
columns.comment: The entity's type (entity.type), so a type filter seeks only its own lanes.

columns.name: property
columns.comment: The property the value is asserted with (search_property.id).

columns.name: language_rank
columns.comment: The language's rank among the values' languages by LANGUAGE_RANKING (browl.names.language_rank), from 0; languages that rank alike, such as unlisted ones, share one.

columns.name: word
columns.comment: 0 for the whole value's row, 1 for a word row, keyed from a later word start; a query reads word lanes after every whole-value lane, so matches from a value's start rank first.

columns.name: length
columns.comment: The key's length in characters (the normalized value's, from the word on for a word row), counted in Python, up to KEY_CHARS.

columns.name: normalized
columns.comment: The key: the value normalized for search (browl.names.normalize), from the word on for a word row, its first KEY_CHARS characters.

columns.name: value
columns.comment: The value's lexical form, its first KEY_CHARS characters; a word row holds no more, and a hit reads the rest from annotation_value.

columns.name: entity
columns.comment: The entity (entity.id).

columns.name: normalized_rest
columns.comment: The key's characters after the first KEY_CHARS, up to MAX_QUERY_CHARS in all for a word row; NULL if there are none.

columns.name: value_rest
columns.comment: The value's characters after the first KEY_CHARS; NULL if there are none, and for word rows.

columns.name: language
columns.comment: The value's language tag, lowercased; NULL if it has none.

columns.name: word_start
columns.comment: Where the key starts in the normalized value: 0 for the whole value's row, else the word's offset, so a hit can mark the word in the value it shows. It's in the key, so a value's word rows never merge.

indexes.name: sqlite_autoindex_search_value_1
indexes.def: PRIMARY KEY (type, property, language_rank, word, length, normalized, value, entity, word_start)

constraints.name: sqlite_autoindex_search_value_1
constraints.def: PRIMARY KEY (type, property, language_rank, word, length, normalized, value, entity, word_start)

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE search_value (
    type TEXT NOT NULL,
    property INTEGER NOT NULL,
    language_rank INTEGER NOT NULL,
    word INTEGER NOT NULL,
    length INTEGER NOT NULL,
    normalized TEXT NOT NULL,
    value TEXT NOT NULL,
    entity INTEGER NOT NULL,
    normalized_rest TEXT,
    value_rest TEXT,
    language TEXT,
    word_start INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (type, property, language_rank, word, length, normalized, value, entity, word_start)
) WITHOUT ROWID

tables.name: search_lane
tables.comment: The lanes of search_value: each (type, property, language_rank, word) group that has rows, with its longest value's length. A query seeks only lanes that exist, and no lengths past a lane's longest.

columns.name: type
columns.comment: The entities' type (entity.type).

columns.name: property
columns.comment: The property (search_property.id).

columns.name: language_rank
columns.comment: The languages' rank (search_value.language_rank).

columns.name: word
columns.comment: 0 for whole values' rows, 1 for word rows (search_value.word).

columns.name: max_length
columns.comment: The lane's longest search_value.length, so at most KEY_CHARS.

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE search_lane (
    type TEXT NOT NULL,
    property INTEGER NOT NULL,
    language_rank INTEGER NOT NULL,
    word INTEGER NOT NULL,
    max_length INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (type, property, language_rank, word)
) WITHOUT ROWID

tables.name: common_value
tables.comment: The common name-like values (browl.search.COMMON_SHARE): each on more than that share of the ontology's entities, and on at least browl.search.COMMON_MIN, so too common to tell entities apart. They get no search_value rows, only these counts, one row per entity type they're on, which the results page shows instead of listing the entities; stored in key order.

columns.name: property
columns.comment: The property it's asserted with (search_property.id).

columns.name: value
columns.comment: The value's lexical form, in any language.

columns.name: type
columns.comment: An entity type it's on (entity.type).

columns.name: normalized
columns.comment: The value normalized for search (browl.names.normalize), which a query matches as search_value's keys.

columns.name: entities
columns.comment: How many entities of that type have it.

columns.name: of_type
columns.comment: How many entities that type has, for the share.

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE common_value (
    property INTEGER NOT NULL,
    value TEXT NOT NULL,
    type TEXT NOT NULL,
    normalized TEXT NOT NULL,
    entities INTEGER NOT NULL,
    of_type INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (property, value, type)
) WITHOUT ROWID

tables.name: edge
tables.comment: The hierarchies' named direct parent-child edges, between equivalence-group representatives, stored in key order.

columns.name: hierarchy
columns.comment: Which hierarchy, named by its entities' type (entity.type), e.g. class or object_property.

columns.name: parent
columns.comment: The parent (entity.id).

columns.name: child
columns.comment: The child (entity.id).

indexes.name: edge_child
indexes.def: CREATE INDEX edge_child ON edge (hierarchy, child)

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE edge (
    hierarchy TEXT NOT NULL,
    parent INTEGER NOT NULL,
    child INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (hierarchy, parent, child)
) WITHOUT ROWID

tables.name: equiv_group
tables.comment: Groups of named classes linked by owl:equivalentClass (union-find), and of a hierarchy's entities in a cycle of edges. Only groups of more than one entity have rows; any other entity is its own representative.

columns.name: entity
columns.comment: An entity in a group (entity.id).

columns.name: representative
columns.comment: The group's representative (entity.id), its first IRI, which stands for the group in edge and counts.

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE equiv_group (
    entity INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    representative INTEGER NOT NULL
)

tables.name: counts
tables.comment: Each hierarchy node's numbers of children and of distinct descendants (DESIGN.md 2.5): a row for every entity of the hierarchy's type that is a group's representative or in no group, except owl:Thing and the other top and bottom entities.

columns.name: hierarchy
columns.comment: Which hierarchy, as in edge.hierarchy.

columns.name: node
columns.comment: The node (entity.id).

columns.name: children
columns.comment: How many immediate children it has.

columns.name: descendants
columns.comment: How many distinct descendants it has, each counted once however many paths lead to it.

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE counts (
    hierarchy TEXT NOT NULL,
    node INTEGER NOT NULL,
    children INTEGER NOT NULL,
    descendants INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (hierarchy, node)
) WITHOUT ROWID

tables.name: root
tables.comment: Each hierarchy's roots, the nodes (as in counts) with no parent in edge, which the tree pages start from (DESIGN.md 2.13), stored in key order.

columns.name: hierarchy
columns.comment: Which hierarchy, as in edge.hierarchy.

columns.name: node
columns.comment: The root (entity.id).

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE root (
    hierarchy TEXT NOT NULL,
    node INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (hierarchy, node)
) WITHOUT ROWID

tables.name: usage_root
tables.comment: The blank-node owner map's roots (P-27, DESIGN.md 2.5, browl.precache.owner_map): the axioms that reach entities through blank nodes (class expressions, lists, annotations on reified axioms), by the top-level triple, reified axiom or unlinked blank node each hangs from. Only roots that are some entity's usage (usage_ref) are kept.

columns.name: id
columns.comment: The root's number, dense.

columns.name: kind
columns.comment: What it is (browl.derived.UsageRootKind): triple, a triple from an IRI to a blank node (owner predicate _:label); axiom, a reified axiom (owl:Axiom), with the annotations on it; general, a blank node nothing links to, with no owner (a general class axiom, an n-ary axiom, a negative property assertion, a SWRL rule).

columns.name: label
columns.comment: The root's blank node, by its label in the store (Jena's afn:bnode), which a query can name as <_:label>.

columns.name: owner
columns.comment: The entity whose axiom it is (entity.id, its IRI's first): a triple's subject, a reified axiom's owl:annotatedSource; NULL if that's no entity (owner_iri) or there's none.

columns.name: owner_iri
columns.comment: The owner's IRI, if it's no entity (an individual, an undeclared IRI); else NULL.

columns.name: predicate
columns.comment: A triple's predicate, or a reified axiom's owl:annotatedProperty; NULL for a general root.

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE usage_root (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    kind TEXT NOT NULL,
    label TEXT NOT NULL,
    owner INTEGER,
    owner_iri TEXT,
    predicate TEXT
)

tables.name: usage_ref
tables.comment: Which roots are which entities' usages, stored in key order: a root is a usage of each entity it names, except its owner and those whose own axiom it is, which their Overview lists (DESIGN.md 2.5).

columns.name: entity
columns.comment: The entity (entity.id, its IRI's first).

columns.name: root
columns.comment: The root (usage_root.id).

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE usage_ref (
    entity INTEGER NOT NULL,
    root INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (entity, root)
) WITHOUT ROWID

tables.name: usage_blank
tables.comment: Per entity, the triples with a blank subject that have it as object or predicate, which usage counts take from Fuseki's unfiltered counts (browl.usages.count_usages). Entities with none have no row.

columns.name: entity
columns.comment: The entity (entity.id, its IRI's first).

columns.name: object
columns.comment: How many triples with a blank subject have it as object.

columns.name: predicate
columns.comment: How many triples with a blank subject have it as predicate.

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE usage_blank (
    entity INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    object INTEGER NOT NULL,
    predicate INTEGER NOT NULL
)

tables.name: hash_prefix
tables.comment: Every distinct URL path that has hash entities (entity.fragment not NULL) under it, for the hash-IRI script (U-13), stored in key order.

columns.name: path
columns.comment: The URL path, as in entity.path.

tables.name: prefix
tables.comment: CURIE prefixes, for entity.curie: the built-in ones, overridden by those the ontology file declares, overridden by EXTRA_PREFIXES.

columns.name: prefix
columns.comment: The prefix name; empty for the default prefix.

columns.name: namespace
columns.comment: The namespace IRI it stands for.

indexes.name: prefix_name
indexes.def: CREATE INDEX prefix_name ON prefix (prefix COLLATE NOCASE, prefix)

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE prefix (
    prefix TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    namespace TEXT NOT NULL
) WITHOUT ROWID

tables.name: type_count
tables.comment: How many entities entity holds of each type, for the home page (U-1), so it needn't count them on every view. A punned IRI counts once for each of its types; a type with no entities has no row.

columns.name: type
columns.comment: The entity type, as in entity.type.

columns.name: count
columns.comment: How many entities have it.

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE type_count (
    type TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    count INTEGER NOT NULL
) WITHOUT ROWID

tables.name: axiom_count
tables.comment: How many of the ontology's own axioms, without its imports, there are of each kind, for the home page (U-1), counted from its triples by OWL 2's mapping to RDF (browl.precache.axiom_counts).

columns.name: kind
columns.comment: The kind: logical, declaration, annotation (assertions and annotation property axioms) or datatype_definition.

columns.name: count
columns.comment: How many axioms there are of it.

tables.def:
CREATE TABLE axiom_count (
    kind TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    count INTEGER NOT NULL
) WITHOUT ROWID
